# Adaptive prefix-cover acquisition: scoped cost theorem and review

28 October 2026. Ordinary proof only; no new Monte Carlo execution and no
change to the existing balanced-tape acquisition or its receipts.

**Conclusion.** The proposed zero-terminal algorithm and its
\(C_{\epsilon/2}\)-dependent cost bound are correct. The adaptive node
selection does not invalidate the confidence guarantee when each selected
word receives a fresh fixed batch. Minimality is particularly simple:
the minimum cover is the unique tree that stops at the first sufficiently
small-survival prefix.

Two optional refinements are substantive. Summable conditional confidence
spending also gives almost-sure termination and an unconditional expected
cost bound when the comparison cover is finite. If terminal predictions
may be nonzero interval midpoints, the same accuracy can instead be tied
to \(C_\epsilon\).

## 1. Definitions and statistical interface

Let \(\mathcal A\) be a finite alphabet of size \(q\ge1\). For a word \(w\),
let \(f(w)\in[0,1]\) be its survival probability from the fixed preparation,
with \(f(\varnothing)=1\). Irreversible absorption gives

\[
 f(wu)\le f(w)
\]

for every extension \(u\). This prefix monotonicity is the only structural
property needed for the cover and cost theorem. Selfadjointness and the
common order vector belong to the separate theorem that obtains a finite
switched tail from primitive repetitions.

A finite full \(q\)-ary prefix tree contains its root and every child of
each nonterminal node. It is an \(\eta\)-cover if every terminal word has
true survival at most \(\eta\). Let \(C_\eta\) be its minimum number of
nodes, or infinity if no finite cover exists. Root is included.

At each selected nonroot word, a trial starts from a genuine fresh
preparation and supplies a Bernoulli indicator with mean \(f(w)\).
Conditional on the history selecting that word, its batch consists of
independent such trials. The word and batch size are fixed before its
batch is inspected. Physical execution may stop after confirmed absorption:
the full-word indicator is then known to be zero.

This is a fresh-batch theorem. Applying its visit-index confidence budget
retroactively to prefixes selected after inspecting an existing shared
data set would require a different selection argument. The existing

# Scoped review of the fresh adaptive-prefix comparator

## Verdict

`core/adaptive_coarse_cover.py` passes the new acquisition, confidence-budget, queue and resource-ledger review. It executes an ordinary adaptive-prefix comparator on the same private source and coarse alive/absorbed interface, using independent fresh data and no lifetime pilot or earlier receipts.

The completed cover has 38 nodes, maximum depth five, 18 branch nodes and 20 terminal nodes. It supplies the stated all-word absolute survival error of 1/16 at failure probability at most 0.001 through the already accepted midpoint-terminal theorem. This review checks that theorem's new operational and statistical inputs; it does not re-audit the theorem or the earlier balanced-cover acquisition.

An independent exact replay verified all 38 batch budgets, every recorded node and queue decision, and all source costs. **No trajectories were generated.**

## Predictable selection and fresh confidence budgets

The queue selects the next word using only previously completed batches. Before requesting any observations for selected node j, the program fixes that word and pays a batch of

\[
N_j=\left\lceil\frac{2}{\epsilon^2}
\log\frac{2j(j+1)}{\delta}\right\rceil,
\qquad \epsilon=1/16,\quad\delta=1/1000.
\]

Every trial in this batch receives a fresh preparation. Conditional on the earlier history, the selected word is fixed and the batch's endpoint survival indicators are independent Bernoulli samples of its true survival probability. A trajectory absorbed before the word ends is a zero in the fixed denominator N_j; it is not removed from the statistic.

Conditional two-sided Hoeffding gives

\[
\Pr\{|\widehat f_j-f(w_j)|>\epsilon/2\mid\text{prior history}\}
\le 2e^{-N_j\epsilon^2/2}
\le\frac{\delta}{j(j+1)}.
\]

The selected word may vary with the earlier data; predictable selection does not invalidate this conditional statement. The deterministic allocation sums to delta over all possible j. Hence the random number of selected nodes and the data-dependent stopping of the queue are covered without a predeclared maximum node count. The reported confidence is the global delta bound; it is not obtained by substituting the observed node count into a post hoc confidence formula.

# Stronger adaptive prefix acquisition on the same source

29 October 2026, Brisbane. A separate acquisition now executes the ordinary
adaptive prefix method on the same countable source as
COARSE_SWITCHING_THEORY.md. It uses independent new observations, without
the earlier receipts or lifetime pilot, and certifies the same all-word
unconditional survival accuracy with fewer source operations.

## Procedure and confidence

The source, common preparation and live/absorbed interface are unchanged.
Every trial starts from a fresh preparation. The acquisition never treats
a surviving coarse label as a restart or requests a microscopic identity.

For epsilon=1/16 and delta=1/1000, select the next word using previous
batches. Before acquiring its new observations, fix batch size

    N_j=ceil(2 epsilon^-2 log(2j(j+1)/delta)).

An upper rational logarithm rounds this paid budget safely. Form the
empirical interval [L,U]=[p_hat-epsilon/2,p_hat+epsilon/2], clipped to [0,1].
If U<=2epsilon, mark that prefix terminal and predict U/2 on it and every
extension. Otherwise predict its interval midpoint at that word and enqueue
both children. Root survival is exactly one.

Conditional on the preceding history, the selected word and sample count
are already fixed and the samples are fresh Bernoulli trials. Hoeffding
spends at most delta/[j(j+1)]. Summing this budget over all potential visit
indices gives simultaneous confidence even for a random final queue length.
This is not a retroactive allocation to prefixes selected from old data.

Branch midpoint error is at most epsilon/2. After a terminal prefix,
irreversible absorption keeps all future survival in [0,U]; the constant
prediction U/2 therefore has error at most epsilon. A complete finite tree
covers every word. The cost and almost-sure termination proof, including
rare confidence failures, is preserved in
branches/scalar/ADAPTIVE_PREFIX_COVER_COST_REVIEW.md.
